evals.prompt: I put my Lambda function inside a VPC so it can talk to our RDS PostgreSQL database. To also let the Lambda call S3 and DynamoDB, I placed the Lambda inside our 'Public Subnet' (whose route table points `0.0.0.0/0` directly to our Internet Gateway `igw-12345`) and enabled 'Auto-assign public IPv4 address' on the subnet. Why is my Lambda STILL timing out with zero logs when calling S3 and DynamoDB, and how do I fix S3 and DynamoDB access for $0?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill, explains that AWS Lambda **Hyperplane ENIs** inside a VPC **never receive public IPv4 addresses**—even in a subnet with `MapPublicIpOnLaunch` and a `0.0.0.0/0 -> igw-xxxx` route, so the Internet Gateway silently drops all outbound packets; and shows fixing S3 and DynamoDB connectivity for **$0.00** by moving Lambda to private subnets and attaching free **VPC Gateway Endpoints** (`com.amazonaws.<region>.s3` and `com.amazonaws.<region>.dynamodb`, `VpcEndpointType: Gateway`) to the private route tables.
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and explains that Lambda Hyperplane ENIs never receive public IPv4 addresses, so routing `0.0.0.0/0` directly to an Internet Gateway (`igw-xxxx`) blackholes all traffic

Recommends moving the Lambda function to private subnets and provisioning free VPC Gateway Endpoints (`com.amazonaws.<region>.s3` and `com.amazonaws.<region>.dynamodb`, `VpcEndpointType: Gateway`) at $0.00 cost
Provides the `AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint` configuration associating both Gateway Endpoints with the private subnet `RouteTableIds`

evals.prompt: I am new to AWS and building a serverless app where my Lambda functions read/write to Amazon DynamoDB, upload PDFs to Amazon S3, push jobs to Amazon SQS, and call the public Stripe API. A coworker told me that for security we must put all our Lambda functions inside a private VPC and create NAT Gateways. Should I put these Lambda functions inside a VPC? Explain why or why not and what it would cost.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill, walks through Priority 1 of the Serverless VPC FinOps Decision Gate (**Do NOT attach Lambda to a VPC** when the function only accesses DynamoDB, S3, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Bedrock, or public APIs), explains that Lambda outside a VPC already runs in an AWS-managed isolated network with public internet access and IAM/TLS/KMS security at **$0.00** networking cost, and warns that putting it in a VPC strips public internet access and would force paying `~$32.40/month per AZ` + `$0.045/GB` for NAT Gateways to reach Stripe and SQS.
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and explicitly advises NOT attaching the Lambda functions to a VPC because they have no private VPC dependencies (RDS, ElastiCache, MSK, internal IPs)
Explains that attaching Lambda to a VPC strips its default public internet access because Hyperplane ENIs do not receive public IPv4 addresses
Warns of the unnecessary NAT Gateway cost (`~$32.40/month per AZ` / `$0.045/hr` + `$0.045/GB` processed) that would be incurred if placed in a VPC

evals.prompt: Can you check our AWS account in ap-south-1 in read-only mode to see what VPCs, Subnets, Route Tables, NAT Gateways, and VPC Endpoints currently exist, and present the 5-Tier Serverless VPC FinOps Decision Gate table?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill, uses connected AWS MCP tools in read-only mode to inspect VPCs, Subnets, Route Tables, NAT Gateways, and VPC Endpoints in `ap-south-1` (accurately reporting the live inventory without fabricating IDs), and presents the 5-Tier Serverless VPC FinOps Decision Gate table (1. No VPC -> $0, 2. S3/DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints -> $0, 3. 1–3 AWS Services Interface Endpoints -> ~$7.20/mo/AZ + $0.01/GB, 4. Dual-Stack IPv6 EIGW -> $0, 5. NAT Gateway -> ~$32.40/mo/AZ + $0.045/GB).
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and uses connected AWS MCP tools in read-only mode to list VPCs, NAT Gateways, or VPC Endpoints in `ap-south-1`
Accurately reports the live networking resources in `ap-south-1` without fabricating VPC IDs or endpoints

Presents the 5-priority Serverless VPC FinOps Decision Gate comparing Gateway Endpoints ($0), Interface Endpoints (`~$7.20/mo/AZ` + `$0.01/GB`), IPv6 EIGW ($0), and NAT Gateways (`~$32.40/mo/AZ` + `$0.045/GB`)

evals.prompt: My Lambda function is inside a private VPC in ap-south-1 because it queries an internal ElastiCache Redis cluster, and it also needs to call external HTTPS APIs and AWS endpoints that support IPv6. I don't want to pay $65/month for two NAT Gateways. How can I give my VPC Lambda free outbound internet access over IPv6?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill, recommends Priority 4 of the FinOps Decision Gate (**Dual-Stack Subnet + Egress-Only Internet Gateway (EIGW)** at **$0.00/month** fixed cost), and provides the SAM/CloudFormation configuration (`AWS::EC2::EgressOnlyInternetGateway`, an `AWS::EC2::Route` with `DestinationIpv6CidrBlock: '::/0'` pointing to the EIGW on the private route table, and `Ipv6AllowedForDualStack: true` inside the Lambda function's `VpcConfig`).
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and recommends Dual-Stack private subnets with an Egress-Only Internet Gateway (`AWS::EC2::EgressOnlyInternetGateway`) at $0.00 monthly gateway cost
Shows adding the IPv6 default route (`DestinationIpv6CidrBlock: '::/0'`) pointing to the `EgressOnlyInternetGatewayId` in the private route table
Shows enabling `Ipv6AllowedForDualStack: true` under `VpcConfig` on the `AWS::Serverless::Function` resource

evals.prompt: We provisioned an `AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint` of type `Interface` for `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.secretsmanager` and an RDS PostgreSQL instance in our private subnets, but our VPC Lambda still times out when calling `boto3.client('secretsmanager').get_secret_value()` and cannot connect to RDS on port 5432. In our template, `PrivateDnsEnabled` was set to `false` on the Interface Endpoint, the Lambda Security Group has `SecurityGroupEgress: []`, and the RDS Security Group only allows inbound `5432` from `10.0.0.0/24` (AZ1 only). Diagnose all three networking bugs and provide the fixes.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and diagnoses all three bugs: (1) `PrivateDnsEnabled: true` must be enabled on the VPC Interface Endpoint (alongside `EnableDnsSupport` and `EnableDnsHostnames` on the VPC) so standard SDK calls to `secretsmanager.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com` resolve to the private endpoint ENI IP, (2) the Lambda Security Group egress must allow outbound TCP `443` (to the Interface Endpoint SG) and TCP `5432` (to the RDS SG), and (3) the RDS and Interface Endpoint Security Groups should allow inbound traffic from the **Lambda Security Group ID** (`SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref LambdaSG`) rather than a single-AZ subnet CIDR block.
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and explains that `PrivateDnsEnabled: true` is required on the Interface Endpoint so the standard AWS SDK hostname resolves to the private ENI IPs
Fixes the Lambda Security Group egress rules to allow outbound TCP `443` (HTTPS for VPC Endpoints) and TCP `5432` (PostgreSQL)
Recommends referencing `SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref LambdaSG` on the RDS and Interface Endpoint inbound security group rules rather than a single-AZ CIDR block

evals.prompt: We have a VPC-attached Lambda in 2 Availability Zones in ap-south-1 (connected to Aurora) that also calls S3, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, and KMS, transferring 200 GB/month to S3 and 5 GB/month to Secrets Manager/KMS. Compare the exact monthly cost of Option A (2 NAT Gateways across 2 AZs for everything) vs Option B (free Gateway Endpoints for S3 + DynamoDB, plus PrivateLink Interface Endpoints across 2 AZs for Secrets Manager and KMS). At how many Interface Endpoint services does a NAT Gateway break even?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and computes the FinOps math across 2 AZs: Option A (2 NAT Gateways = `2 * $32.40 = $64.80/mo` fixed + `205 GB * $0.045/GB = $9.23` data processing = **`$74.03/mo`**), vs Option B (S3 + DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints = **`$0.00`** for both fixed and the 200 GB S3 transfer, plus 2 Interface Endpoints across 2 AZs = `2 services * 2 AZs * $7.20/mo ($0.01/hr) = $28.80/mo` fixed + `5 GB * $0.01/GB = $0.05` = **`$28.85/mo`**, saving `~$45.18/mo` / 61%), and notes that at `$7.20/AZ/service` vs `$32.40/AZ` per NAT Gateway, Interface Endpoints are cheaper for **1 to 4 AWS services** (`4 * $7.20 = $28.80 < $32.40`), whereas `>= 5` Interface Endpoint services exceed a NAT Gateway's fixed hourly cost.
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and calculates Option A's 2-AZ NAT Gateway cost (`2 * $32.40 = $64.80/mo` fixed + `205 GB * $0.045/GB = $9.23` = `~$74.03/mo`)

Calculates Option B's cost using free S3/DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints (`$0.00` for the 200 GB S3 transfer) plus 2 Interface Endpoints across 2 AZs (`2 * 2 * $7.20 = $28.80/mo` + `5 GB * $0.01/GB = $0.05` = `~$28.85/mo`)

Identifies the Interface Endpoint vs NAT Gateway break-even threshold (~4 AWS services per AZ at `$7.20/AZ/service` vs `$32.40/AZ` for a NAT Gateway) and reminds setting `PrivateDnsEnabled: true` on Interface Endpoints

evals.prompt: Our team deployed 18 microservices (each with its own VPC-attached Lambda function and distinct Security Group) into two tiny `/28` private subnets (`16` total IPs, `11` usable IPs per subnet after AWS reserves 5 IPs) in ap-south-1. During a deployment, new Lambda functions failed with `EC2ThrottledException` / `InvalidSubnetException: The specified subnet does not have enough freeonio addresses`. Explain how AWS Lambda Hyperplane ENIs share IPs across functions vs Security Groups, why `/28` subnets caused IP exhaustion, and how to size Multi-AZ private subnets.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill, explains AWS Lambda **Hyperplane ENI** mechanics: Lambda shares a Hyperplane ENI across concurrent executions that share the exact same **`(SubnetId, SecurityGroupIds)` tuple**, meaning 18 functions each with a *distinct* Security Group require at least 18+ separate Hyperplane ENIs per subnet (exceeding the 11 usable IPs in a `/28` subnet, since AWS reserves 5 IPs per subnet), and recommends consolidating shared Security Groups by access tier and provisioning at least **2 private subnets across distinct AZs with `/24` (`251` usable IPs) or larger CIDR blocks**.
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and explains that AWS Hyperplane ENIs are shared per unique `(SubnetId, SecurityGroupIds)` combination, so assigning 18 distinct Security Groups creates at least 18 separate ENIs per subnet
Explains why `/28` subnets (`16 - 5 AWS-reserved = 11` usable IPs) suffer immediate IP exhaustion during deployments and scaling
Recommends provisioning Multi-AZ private subnets with `/24` (or larger) CIDR blocks and consolidating Lambda Security Groups by logical access boundary

evals.prompt: We are deploying a fleet of **Lambda MicroVMs** (`Runtime: microvm`) that need to reach up to 800 concurrent active MicroVMs while calling an internal Aurora database and external HTTPS APIs. Unlike standard Lambda, when we omitted `VpcConfig`, the MicroVMs had zero internet connectivity! Explain why Lambda MicroVMs have no internet access by default, how **Lambda Network Connectors (LNCs)** work (`Gbps` bandwidth and concurrent MicroVMs per LNC), and how many subnets/LNCs are required for 800 concurrent MicroVMs.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill, explains Section 5: unlike standard Lambda functions, **Lambda MicroVMs have NO internet or VPC access by default** unless `VpcConfig` is attached; attaching `VpcConfig` provisions **Lambda Network Connectors (LNCs)** (**2 LNCs per subnet for HA**, **20 Gbps** bandwidth per LNC, supporting up to **250 concurrent MicroVMs per LNC** = 500 per subnet), and shows configuring at least **2 private `/24` (or larger) subnets across distinct AZs** (4 LNCs total = up to 1,000 concurrent MicroVM capacity, covering the 800 concurrent MicroVMs with HA) routed via VPC Endpoints / NAT Gateways.
expectations: Activates the serverless-vpc-and-private-networking skill and explains that Lambda MicroVMs have NO outbound internet or VPC access by default unless `VpcConfig` is configured
States the exact Lambda Network Connector (LNC) specifications: 2 LNCs provisioned per subnet for HA, 20 Gbps bandwidth each, and up to 250 concurrent MicroVMs per LNC
Calculates that 800 concurrent MicroVMs require at least 4 LNCs across at least 2 Multi-AZ private subnets (`/24` or larger CIDR blocks) with VPC Endpoints or NAT Gateways for outbound routing
